record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a finite directed graph, and let lambda(G) be the number of vertices in a longest directed path of G. For every natural number q with 0 < q < lambda(G), must the vertices of G be partitionable into two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs A and B such that lambda(A) equals q and lambda(B) equals lambda(G) - q?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 Let G be a directed graph. For every natural number q with 0 < q < λ(G) there is a partition (A, B) of G such that λ(A) = q and λ(B) = λ(G) − q.
It seems that this conjecture has not been studied in literature yet.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite directed graph (digraph) on a vertex set $V(G)$. A directed path in $G$ is a sequence of distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \dots, v_k$ such that $(v_i, v_{i+1})$ is an arc of $G$ for $i = 1, \dots, k-1$; its number of vertices is $k$. Define $\lambda(G)$ to be the maximum number of vertices in any directed path of $G$. For a subset $S \subseteq V(G)$, let $G[S]$ denote the induced subdigraph on $S$, and write $\lambda(S) := \lambda(G[S])$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: for every finite directed graph $G$ and every integer $q$ with $0 < q < \lambda(G)$, there exists a partition $V(G) = A \sqcup B$ into two disjoint (possibly empty) subsets such that
$$\lambda(A) = q \quad \text{and} \quad \lambda(B) = \lambda(G) - q.$$
artifact.status_search_result: This is the strong form of Berge's path partition conjecture for digraphs (1982). It is known to hold for q=1 (Gallai–Milgram), for q=2 (proved by Hartman), and for q ≥ λ(G)−3, as well as for acyclic digraphs and several restricted classes (e.g., claw-free digraphs). The full conjecture remains open for general digraphs.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Berge's strong path partition conjecture for k=2
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of Berge's strong path partition conjecture for k=2.
status_evidence.claim: The strong version of Berge's path partition conjecture is established for q=2 but remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: Some digraph classes that meet the directed path partition conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: DPPC states: For every digraph D and any choice of positive integer q < λ(D), there exists a partition (A, B) of D such that λ(D[A]) ≤ q and λ(D[B]) ≤ λ(D) − q.
status_evidence.claim: The directed path partition conjecture is known only for restricted digraph classes.

status_evidence.title: On The Strong and the Semi-Strong Path Partition Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: On The Strong and the Semi-Strong Path Partition Conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The strong path partition conjecture is studied and remains partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Berge's path partition conjecture for k ≥ λ−3
status_evidence.snippet: Proof of Berge's path partition conjecture for k ≥ λ−3.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is verified for q within 3 of λ(G).
